- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then gradually converges toward true values.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 47.00, 49.61) and fail to adjust downward quickly enough.
- Model exhibits persistent upward bias in the middle to late forecast window (days 15–25), often failing to reflect mean reversion toward lower levels.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day window, suggesting lag in capturing short-term volatility or sudden policy/spot market shifts.
- Model underestimates true outcomes when prices dip below 40.00, particularly in the first 10 days of the forecast window.
- Forecasts show a tendency to smooth out sharp declines or spikes, leading to underestimation of volatility in the first 5–10 days.
- Model fails to account for sudden downward corrections after high peaks (e.g., 49.61 → 47.00), often missing the “rebound” or “reversion” phase.
- Forecast accuracy improves as the horizon moves toward the end of the 30-day window, suggesting model is better at capturing long-term trends than short-term shocks.
